vision.title: RiffSync
vision.mission: RiffSync is an open-source fan catalog and realtime watch-party companion for riff-style episodic comedy: browse curated entries anonymously or gather on a canonical room page where a **signed-in** host drives an official YouTube embed and may share that viewing surface with guests via browser realtime media—coordinating chat and room lifecycle lawfully without operating a communal video vault.
vision.core_purpose: Serve fans of MST-inspired commentary tracks by pairing a persisted episode catalog with room-centric viewing: a **signed-in** host opens a shared room URL, drives the official embedded player—**can change the episode in-room via a catalog-backed picker**—and broadcasts captured audio/video so guests (typically anonymous) see one shared picture—including matched ad cadence—rather than parallel embeds manually aligned in time. Lobby discovery, room-scoped chat, presence-friendly anonymous display names for guests, and stable shareable URLs support repeat community drop-ins. Playback expectations use a host self-report of Premium versus ad-supported experience; the platform does not verify YouTube entitlement. TMDB-derived imagery and synopsis-style copy are attributed and reconciled; thumbnails may reference optional YouTube fields from the same reconcile path. Operators maintain catalog quality, curated collections, and roster visibility through separate staff tooling, with health and misuse signals framed around CloudWatch. The roadmap preserves a pluggable lawful playback boundary (including eventual alternate backends and viewer-local Chromecast) without operating a centralized piracy archive.
vision.key_architecture: Baseline delivery favors AWS serverless patterns expressed through **AWS CDK** infrastructure (recommended **CDK app in TypeScript**), with synchronous HTTP routes and a WebSockets channel for realtime room events backed by DynamoDB-shaped persistence, Lambda handlers implemented in **TypeScript** targeting **Node.js**, optional EventBridge- or Scheduler-driven housekeeping, Secrets Manager where needed, and CloudWatch-centric metrics, dashboards, and log-driven investigation paths for operators—aligned with **Cognito JWT** for **hosting** paths (Facebook or other IdP optional per product) while keeping **guest browse/join/watch** workable **without** mandatory signup. Prefer managed APIs and data stores over always-on compute containers unless justified. Catalog and reconcile jobs integrate TMDB for poster, backdrop, tagline, and overview fields alongside optional thumbnail URLs grounded in reconcile output. Separation between coordination state and playback source stays explicit so lawful non-YouTube backends can integrate later.

strategic_goals.short_term: Deliver an MVP where guests stay anonymous-first (browse, join, chat, watch) while **hosting** requires signed-in identity (**Cognito `sub` / `hostSub`): seeded catalog, room pages with lawful embed + optional WebRTC broadcast, resilient room lifecycle, lobby discovery, advisory Premium versus ad-supported labels, canonical share URLs, and documentation covering attribution, capture consent, embedding limits, and hosting gates.
strategic_goals.medium_term: Mature operator admin for catalog authoring, curated lists, and roster insight; deepen observability narratives for staff investigations; optionally ship Facebook-mediated continuity without weakening optional-auth posture; tighten moderation primitives around opaque session identifiers; and stabilize optional per-viewer casting patterns where browsers and embed rules cooperate.
strategic_goals.long_term: Extend to additional lawful playback surfaces and purchase-respecting or self-hosted media paths without becoming a communal re-upload depot; broaden contributor and self-hosted operator narratives; pursue Chromecast and alternate backends only where Terms of Service, purchase rights, and platform rules remain intact.

key_principles.text: Respect Terms of Service and rules of third parties: lawful YouTube iframe usage, honoring embed eligibility and takedowns, honest handling of autoplay constraints, Cast behavior governed by Google and partner rules, clear TMDB attribution, and no stripping ads or circumventing normal playback mechanics.

Operate as unofficial fan tooling with transparent disclaimers versus MST3K-adjacent rights holders and YouTube itself; naming, marketing, and in-product copy avoid implying endorsement or partnership.

Never position the community as owners of uploads to a centralized piracy vault; prefer coordination metadata, catalogs of lawful links or personal-library playback, licensing clarity storytelling, or individually operated libraries over anonymous shared infringing files.

Default to anonymous guest identities (persisted display names per browser/device) for browse/join/watch/chat; **elevated login required to host**—continuity features such as Facebook login must augment rather than block catalog browsing or joining rooms.

Be explicit where the product cannot authenticate reality: playback-experience badges are advisory admin attestations backed by observable behavior in chat and shared viewing, never entitlement guarantees.
Favor observable operations: dashboards, metrics-first reporting, structured logs for operators, so catalog health and incident response stay grounded in telemetry rather than best guesses alone.

competitive_advantages.text: A domain-shaped catalog and room-first navigation where integrated broadcast from the lawful embed preserves shared timing for riff comedy versus forcing each guest to reconcile parallel embed clocks.
A separation between durable room coordination (chat, signaling, discovery, catalog metadata) and peer-mediated media so lawful playback stays transparent while guests receive one shared stream.
An open codebase and seeded JSON catalog trajectory that welcomes contributor improvements, audited metadata, and self-hosted deployments for communities that demand operational control.

An architecture storyline that cleanly separates realtime coordination from the playback spine, enabling lawful experimentation with additional sources or purchaser-only streams without rebranding room-centric shared viewing semantics.

differentiation_from_competitors.text: Unlike generic synced movie extensions, RiffSync foregrounds riff-episode metadata, MST-flavored taxonomy affordances such as curated era lists when operators publish them, and lobby flows tuned to asynchronous fandom timelines rather than sterile conference links.

Compared to manual Discord share-and-countdown sessions, rooms pair catalog-backed URLs with explicit admin-driven playback plus shared media surfaces so jokes land together without informal countdown rituals alone.

Relative to opaque hosted watch apps, RiffSync keeps infrastructure intent transparent: attributable metadata pipelines through TMDB, and paths for operators to evolve catalog policy in the open rather than relying on closed editorial black boxes alone.

Against hypothetical pirate streaming aggregators, the product invests in disclaimers, ToS-aligned embeds only, refusal to centralize user-uploaded infringing assets, and future hooks for purchase-respecting or personal-library playback—all communicated plainly to backers and auditors.
